- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.2) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >70) by overshooting in next period; apply a 1–3% downward correction after a spike.
- In periods with high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.6–0.8 and -0.2 to 0.0), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day mean if sentiment is erratic.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to anticipate further drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows sustained positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.6), model may overfit recent trend; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.
